brief: BCOM has broken out from its long-term trend line and 200-day moving average, dislocating higher after testing that level over the summer. The move is driven by a convergence of supply shocks: Hormuz disruptions hitting fertiliser and feedstock flows, renewed Russia-Ukraine escalation disrupting Black Sea grain exports, and El Nino-linked weather risk tightening global grain balances. Agricultural prices are accelerating as a result, with wheat, rice and sugar all elevated. The note's core mechanism is a policy shock: when drought or supply disruption hits, exporting governments restrict shipments to protect domestic food supply, and global prices move more violently than the underlying crop loss alone would justify. Because US 10-year breakevens have historically moved in close tandem with grains (BCOMGR), continued grain strength could push the inflation narrative into rates. But positioning has turned crowded again, with managed-money net corn longs near 317k contracts after collapsing 88% in three weeks during the June washout, leaving the complex vulnerable to reversals; wheat already faded mid-week after hitting multi-year highs.
